title: A merge refusal must carry git's reason; z23's was empty
description:
z23's attempt was refused with:

    merge_failed: attempt 2 of z23 does not merge onto epic/ncv:

Note the trailing colon with NOTHING after it. The refusal names no file, no conflict, no cause.

git's own output was precise and actionable — six 'file location' conflicts, each naming the source path, the rename, AND the suggested destination:

    CONFLICT (file location): cloud/factory/src/epic-reconciler.ts added in
    origin/z23a2 inside a directory that was renamed in HEAD, suggesting it
    should perhaps be moved to cloudflare/src/epic-reconciler.ts.

That is a diagnosis and a repair instruction in one line, and the reconciler threw it away. An operator reading the feed sees a dead end; an operator who re-runs the merge by hand sees the answer immediately. The gap between those two experiences is the defect.

Worse for unattended operation: a resolve-conflict job dispatched from this refusal would be handed a message with no information in it. The refusal is the ONLY durable record — the worktree is torn down on cleanup.

Work:
- Capture the merge command's stderr and carry it in the refusal, not just the exit status.
- Truncate rather than drop: a long conflict list is still worth its first N lines.
- Cover the empty-reason case with a test that FAILS if the detail is blank — an error message that can be empty will be.

Found on 2026-09-18 resolving z23 in epic ncv.
acceptance_criteria: A merge refusal carries the underlying git conflict output, and a test fails if the reason is empty
